solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Spooner's resentful convicts found down in the dumps

definitions.note: a noun description: things you find down at the rubbish dump

indicators.note: Spooner's tells us to swap the opening sounds of the two words that follow, as the Reverend Spooner famously did

parts.note: a resentful person is bitter
lags is slang for convicts, especially old lags

explanation.surface: Bitter prisoners are depressed, feeling down in the dumps.
explanation.walkthrough: BITTER LAGS with the B and L swapped gives LITTER BAGS. 'Down in the dumps' reads as low spirits but means literally at the tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacks of discarded rubbish are what end up at a refuse tip, so they are things found at the dump.

clue.text: National Inquirer's no.1 serial criminal

indicators.note: the number one letter of the word, i.e. its first, is taken
criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A tabloid newspaper headline about a serial killer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National Inquirer' looks like the US tabloid; 'National' is in fact the definition. 'criminal' shuffles SERIAL into SRAELI.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of a country is one of its nationals, here a citizen of Israel.

clue.text: Waste time being over-hasty

parts.note: rash means acting too hastily

explanation.surface: Rushing things only ends up wasting time.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: rubbish or worthless material is waste, especially in American usage.

clue.text: Embarrassed leaders such as Kinnock and Kennedy?

definitions.note: plural noun: examples of a type of person

parts.note: an embarrassed person goes red
heads are leaders, as in heads of state

explanation.surface: Two party leaders left blushing over some political embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: Neil Kinnock (Labour) and Charles Kennedy (Liberal Democrats) both led British parties and both had red hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: both politicians were famously ginger-haired, so they are instances of people with red hair.

clue.text: Insignificant event preceding tsunami

definitions.meaning: idiom for an amount too small to matter
read literally: a sudden fall of the sea floor, which can set off a giant wave

explanation.surface: A minor tremor before a giant wave hits.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a tiny contribution lost in a vast whole; literally, a sinking of the seabed triggers tsunamis.

clue.text: Working with intelligence, start to plant yard with grass border

indicators.note: grass is said to border the other pieces, lying on both sides of them

parts.note: to grass is to inform on someone, which is also to sing

indicators.note: the start of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A gardening instruction: plant a yard edged with a grass border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass border' looks like a lawn edging; 'grass' is SING (inform) and 'border' puts it around P and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Espionage means gathering secret intelligence, so a spy is at work with intelligence.

clue.text: Nobleman almost naked

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters of the word are removed

parts.note: almost means nearly

explanation.surface: A peer caught with barely any clothes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naked' strips N and Y from the outside of NEARLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a British peer ranking above a viscount and below a marquess.

clue.text: I see actor throwing out collection of arcane items

indicators.note: throwing out suggests the letters are tossed about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone watches a performer being ejected from a cabinet of curiosities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throwing out' looks like a deletion, but nothing is removed: all nine letters of I SEE ACTOR are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the term covers obscure things understood only by a select few.

clue.text: Poor Bobbie regularly given the run around

indicators.note: around tells us the run word goes round the picked letters

parts.note: to rush is to run

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: Unlucky Bobbie keeps being fobbed off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes B, B, I from Bobbie; 'around' puts RUSH around them.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: something of poor quality is described as worthless.

clue.text: Creature seen in our ocean frequently

indicators.note: frequently means at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A sea creature often spotted in our waters.
explanation.definitionFit: The killer whale is an example of a creature, a large marine mammal.

clue.text: Toxic, explosive articles stirring up Brits by Dom

indicators.note: stirring up suggests mixing the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone called Dom is causing trouble among the British with nasty, inflammatory articles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toxic, explosive articles' reads as poisonous journalism but means radiological weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: these weapons pair conventional explosive with radioactive material to spread contamination.

clue.text: Energy saved by support bod working in IT

indicators.note: saved by means held safe inside the other piece

parts.note: a tee is a support for a golf ball
chi (or qi) is the vital energy of Chinese philosophy

explanation.surface: Someone in IT support is trying to save energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support' and 'bod' look like one phrase, IT support person, but 'support' is wordplay (TEE) and the definition is 'bod working in IT'.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal term for a technician or computer specialist, a person employed in computing.

clue.text: Strongly criticise Ms Moore, about to become viral worldwide?

definitions.note: adjective phrase for a noun answer; the question mark flags a cryptic description of a global outbreak

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly, as a reviewer does
Demi Moore is an American actress
C (circa) is the abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: Slamming Demi Moore is set to go viral across the globe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'viral' suggests social media but means an actual virus spreading.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease outbreak that spreads across the whole world is a global epidemic.

clue.text: Notorious individual describing one stuffed with 1?

definitions.meaning: the al-Qaeda leader Osama, a notorious figure
read as two words: a rubbish receptacle loaded with the bags from 1 Across

explanation.surface: Describing a notorious figure as stuffed full of rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Osama, the al-Qaeda founder, was notorious; split, the name reads as a refuse container that is loaded.

clue.text: Copies Riley doing real-time tummy exercise?

definitions.note: verb phrase: does as Riley does, from the idiom 'the life of Riley', a carefree luxurious life

parts.note: live means happening in real time, as a live broadcast
a sit-up exercises the stomach muscles

explanation.surface: Riley is mimicked during a live-streamed workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The life of Riley' is an idiom for a life of ease and luxury.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living the life of Riley enjoys themselves lavishly, so copying Riley means partying and indulging.

clue.text: Leader of Italian resistance unit retired, giving modest address

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
retired means drawn back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the ohm is the unit of electrical resistance

explanation.surface: An Italian resistance leader, now retired, gives a modest speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resistance' suggests partisans but is electrical: OHM, reversed by 'retired' to MHO.
explanation.definitionFit: The texting abbreviation for 'in my humble opinion' is a self-deprecating way to address others.

clue.text: Litter? New duster will collect it

indicators.note: will collect means the anagram gathers the other word inside itself
new signals the letters made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A new duster will pick up the litter.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a housework promise; in fact 'New' makes DETRUS and 'will collect' wraps that round the pronoun, so the duster gathers its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: scattered waste and fragments are rubbish, and litter is an example.

clue.text: Sun's leader, page 4, such a disreputable character!

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: IV is 4 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: The Sun tabloid's page-four story exposes a shady character.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a British slang term for a flashy small-time crook or black-market dealer.

clue.text: Rising salesman Dave struggling to spread effectively

indicators.note: in a down light, rising means read upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters thrashing about into a new order

explanation.surface: A sales rep called Dave rises in the ranks but can't sell well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns REP into PER; 'struggling' rearranges DAVE into VADE.
explanation.definitionFit: To permeate something is to spread through all of it, which is spreading in an effective way.

clue.text: Discuss loftier garret of priests

indicators.note: discuss here signals speaking the words out, so we hear what they sound like

parts.note: loftier means higher; a garret is an attic

explanation.surface: A conversation about a higher attic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'HIGHER ATTIC' said quickly sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to the priesthood, as in the hieratic script used by Egyptian priests.

clue.text: Puttin' down timeless drug

indicators.note: timeless means without T, the abbreviation for time

parts.note: putting down is insulting, with the dropped g mirrored by the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A slangy remark about someone mocking an old-fashioned remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Puttin'' says the final G is dropped, giving INSULTIN; 'timeless' removes a T.
explanation.definitionFit: The hormone treatment for diabetes is a medication, so it counts as a drug.

clue.text: Conclude Bristol is packed with dross

indicators.note: the words are packed with the answer, which sits within them across the word break

explanation.surface: Someone decides Bristol is full of rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: dross is waste matter or rubbish, as are scattered remains and fragments.

clue.text: The Duke of Milan's quite correct to defend son, Oscar

indicators.note: to defend means surround and protect, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: proper means quite correct or fitting
O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An Italian aristocrat is right to protect his son, Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's The Tempest, the exiled magician is the rightful Duke of Milan.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's magician in The Tempest holds the title of Milan's duke, usurped by his brother.

clue.text: France pitching in to recycle garbage

indicators.note: pitching in means the letter is thrown into the middle of the other word

parts.note: to reuse something is to recycle it
F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: France joins in to help recycle rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: household waste and rubbish thrown away is garbage.

clue.text: Deadly river claiming reserves

indicators.note: claiming means taking the other piece into itself

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
the TA, Territorial Army, was the British Army reserve

explanation.surface: A dangerous river that has taken the lives of soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fal is a river in Cornwall in south-west England; the TA was Britain's volunteer army reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something that causes death is lethal or mortal.

clue.text: Bra — letter G — tailored item of ladies underwear

indicators.note: tailored means cut and reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lingerie catalogue listing: a tailored bra in size G.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a band worn round the waist to hold up stockings is a piece of women's lingerie.

clue.text: Hear end of story

indicators.note: hear tells us to listen to how the word sounds

parts.note: a tail is the end of something

explanation.surface: Listen to how the story finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a narrative or yarn is a story.

clue.text: At a knockdown price, Charlie shifted pile

indicators.note: shifted means moved away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: something sold at a knockdown price is cheap
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Charlie sold off a big stack at a bargain price.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a mound or stack of things is a pile.

clue.text: Participates vocally in hairdressing salon gossip

indicators.note: in means the answer lies within the following words

explanation.surface: Someone joins in the chatter at the hair salon.
explanation.definitionFit: To join in a song with others is to take part with one's voice.
